content.title: About
content.content: Bagel with oat bran is a whole‑grain baked product that incorporates oat bran into the dough. It features a crisp crust, a slightly dense crumb, and a subtle nutty aroma from the bran.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oat bran is rich in beta‑glucan, which helps maintain healthy cholesterol levels.
Traditional bagels are boiled before baking, giving them their characteristic chewy texture.
Oat bran is a by‑product of oat processing and is often used to boost the nutritional profile of foods.
Bagels are commonly served with seeds, cheese, or vegetables, but they are also tasty plain.
In recent years, oat‑bran bagels have gained popularity among health‑conscious consumers.

items.title: High in beta‑glucan
items.content: Beta‑glucan can lower LDL cholesterol and supports immune function.

items.title: Rich source of dietary fiber
items.content: Oat bran adds both soluble and insoluble fiber, improving digestion and promoting satiety.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for energy metabolism, muscle function, and nerve health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Bagel with oat bran raises blood sugar more slowly than typical white bakery products.

items.title: B vitamins
items.content: Oat bran provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are important for carbohydrate metabolism and nervous system support.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to oats or oat bran, experiencing skin rashes, itching, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on equipment shared with wheat, so the product may contain trace gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite its fiber content, the bagel is relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is important for weight management.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or heat treatment lowers its level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bagel with oat bran can be enjoyed as a snack, sliced and topped with cream cheese, avocado, or hummus, added to sandwiches, salads, or soups. Toasting it adds a pleasant crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bagels in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent drying out and mold growth. Discard any bagels that develop a stale or off odor.
